literature_notes: All nine ledger lines (L1–L9) report C-terminal 1D4 epitope tags (TETSQVAPA or the 8-aa rhodopsin C-terminal peptide) appended to the full-length melanopsin/OPN4 protein. The authoritative topology places the entire C-terminal region of OPN4 intracellularly (residues 354–478), so every one of these tags faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface. No ledger line reports a tag on the extracellular N-terminus (residues 1–72), in any of the four extracellular loops (ECL1: 130–144; ECL2: 210–236; ECL3: 322–330), or at any other extracellular position. L2 describes a chimeric tail-swap beginning at residue 457Q (also intracellular), not an epitope-tag insertion. L5 covers zebrafish orthologs with C-terminal 1D4 tags (intracellular). L6–L8 cover chimeric RHO/OPN4 constructs whose 1D4 tags are likewise C-terminal and intracellular; the surface immunolabelling in L7–L8 detects the opsin transmembrane body via anti-rhodopsin antibodies, not an extracellular tag. Because no ledger line grounds an extracellular insertion, the correct answer is zero surface sites.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal 1D4 epitope tag appended after the last residue (M478) of full-length human OPN4; the entire C-terminal tail (354–478) is intracellular per topology, so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface. Functional BRET assays confirmed the tagged protein is expressed and functional.

Chimeric hOPN4 construct replaces the C-terminal section from residue 457Q onward with the musOpn4L C-terminal tail; residue 457 is intracellular (topology 354–478). This is a domain-swap, not an epitope-tag insertion, and the position is cytoplasmic.
